_about: Permanent scouting notes learned from post-fight reviews (round-by-round reports, scorecards, recaps, and Suleman's own fight notes). Each note only counts for fights AFTER its date. Tags feed the engine's 'Scouting notes' signal. Add, never rewrite history.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Round by round, Barcelos took him down or swept him to the mat in every round (about seven times) and took his back repeatedly, with RNC and neck-crank threats in R4. Rosas won only R1 on Sherdog's cards, looked spent before R3 (Cageside) and trailed on all three judges' cards entering R5; the finish was an R5 inside trip. The late finish doesn't prove his cardio.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: At 39 he won R2-R4 on all three Sherdog cards and led all three judges entering R5 (Real Combat Media: one judge 10-8 in R4), using body work, repeated trips and takedowns and back control against a much younger, faster striker. He was still scoring takedowns early in R5 before landing awkwardly on Rosas' inside trip.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Dropped by a Bellato left hook late in R1 and survived a rear-naked choke attempt, then won R2 (2 of 3 Sherdog cards) with kicks and clinch work and knocked Bellato out in R3.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Per Sherdog's play-by-play he had just dropped Akylbek with a left hand when he threw the illegal knee that got him disqualified; Akylbek had taken him down earlier in R1. He was on his way to winning when he fouled.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Took Osmanli down early in the TUF 34 final but was dropped by a left hand just before the illegal knee that knocked him out and won him the fight by DQ (Sherdog play-by-play).

Lost R1 and R4 to Pantoja's takedowns and top control but stuffed most other attempts, won R2, R3 and R5 on the feet, and dropped Pantoja with a one-two in R5 as the fresher man. Judges 49-46, 48-47, 50-45; 19 of 20 media scores had him.

His takedowns won R1 and R4 (Sherdog 3-0 both), but his output dropped badly in R5: Van out-landed him at will, dropped him with a one-two and stuffed his late takedowns. He was cut by a head clash in R2.
Knocked out on his feet by Sean Sharaf's first left hook at 0:12, before any wrestling exchange. His first pro loss, in his fifth fight.
Knocked out the unbeaten Gable Steveson with one left hook at 0:12.
Was losing the range battle to Ruffy (low kicks, body jab, a clean right) and his single-leg failed, but he stayed in the clinch hunting elbows and knocked Ruffy out with one at 4:56 of R1.
Won most of R1 at range, then was knocked out by a Tsarukyan elbow at 4:56 after a long stretch of clinch work on the fence.
Won R1 clearly (staggered Menifield, mount and back), then was visibly exhausted from R2 with a broken nose and lost R2-R3 and a split decision.
Staggered by right hands and mounted in R1 while breaking his thumb, he came back to win R2 and R3 with pressure and dirty boxing for a split decision.
Tripped Jourdain off caught kicks three times, dropped him twice in R2 (left uppercut, clinch knee) and stopped him with a left hook to the body in R3, ahead on every card.
Had his kicks caught and was tripped to the mat three times, dropped twice in R2 (uppercut, knee) and quit to a body shot in R3.

Dropped by a Despaigne left hook early in R1 and wobbled several times, then won R2 in the clinch and dropped Despaigne with a leg kick in R3. The split loss wasn't a robbery: 9 of 13 media scores on MMADecisions had Despaigne.
Threw almost nothing in R1 as Shahbazyan chopped his legs, only opened up in R3, and was dropped by a right hand late. All 11 media scores were 30-27 against him.
Backed Osman Diaz to the fence with a long combination, dropped him with an overhand right and finished at 2:04 of R1.
Barely threw for two minutes and was dropped by Delgado in R1 (lost the round on all Sherdog cards), then took over with pressure and a takedown in R2, and dropped and submitted Delgado in R3.
Dropped Jean Silva and won R1 with switch-stance kicks and punch bursts, but faded under pressure, lost R2 and was dropped and choked out in R3.
Split win the media didn't back: Sherdog's three scorers had Morales winning R1-R2 (29-28 Morales) and media split 6-3 for Morales on MMADecisions. His one clear round was R3 on top control.

Lost a split decision (Topps had him 29-28; Bell and Colón 30-27 Moreno) that all three Sherdog scorers and 6 of 9 media had him winning 29-28. He won R1-R2 on Sherdog's cards with right hands, uppercuts, front kicks and knees before being taken down in R3.
Dropped and badly hurt by a Rahiki left hook in R2, he recovered to threaten chokes late in the round, then dropped Rahiki and dominated R3 from top (one judge 10-8).
Dropped McMillen and won R2, but was visibly fatigued late in that round and exhausted in R3, where he was dropped and controlled from top.
Wobbled Fiorot early and dropped her with a counter right hook in R1 (one Sherdog 10-8), out-landed her in R2, then gave up R3 while bleeding from a cut.
Wobbled and dropped by Grasso in R1 and out-worked in R2; came alive only in R3 with side kicks and one-twos.
Won a low-output 29-28 on well-timed takedowns in R1 and R3; did little on the feet and couldn't keep Cortes Acosta down for long. Each judge gave Cortes Acosta a different round.
Out-landed in every round on Sherdog's cards; Martinez's leg kicks left him unsteady on his lead leg by R2 and an overhand right dropped him in R3. Very low output.
Beat veteran Dan Ige in every round on Sherdog's and all 11 media cards: body work, leg kicks that compromised Ige's lead leg and an R3 knockdown.
Dazed early by Chairez in R1, he won R1-R2 with takedowns and heavy ground and pound; tired and hobbled by a kick in R3 but still took Chairez down twice.
His kicking volume beat Salikhov in all three rounds on the judges' cards (30-27, 30-27, 29-28) despite being tripped or taken down six times off caught kicks; staggered Salikhov late in R2.
Caught kicks for six takedowns but did almost nothing from top until the last minute, and lost every round on two judges' cards.
Took Drakkar Klose down and controlled him for two rounds (Sherdog 3/3 both), then mounted, took the back and finished an inverted triangle in R3.
Taken down and controlled by Tommy Gantt for two rounds and submitted from underneath in R3.
Cut early and his pace dropped noticeably in R3, which all three judges and Sherdog gave to Rongzhu.
Six takedowns and 8:51 of control against Antonio Monteiro (DK Network stats); won R1 and R3 on the mat but tired and lost R2.
Taken down six times and controlled for almost nine minutes by Tyshawn Williams; took R2 when Williams tired.
Took Christian Eckerlin down about a minute in, held top position for most of R1, then took the back and finished a rear-naked choke at 4:58.

Taken down early by David Kozma and couldn't get back up in almost four minutes; he cut Kozma from the bottom but gave up his back and tapped to an RNC at 4:58 of R1. His third stoppage loss in his last four fights.
Dropped Christian Jungwirth in R1 (left hand) and R2 (right hook) and won a unanimous decision while fighting through a knee injury from camp.

Knocked down in R1 and R2 by Max Coga but recovered both times, hurt Coga's lead leg with low kicks and pressed hard in R3. Lost a close unanimous decision (29-28, 30-27, 29-28) in the Fight of the Night.

Aged 41 and back from retirement after 469 days out, he took the unbeaten Frederic Vosgröne down repeatedly, defended his leg-lock attempts and finished with ground and pound at 4:50 of R2 (sig. strikes 89-13 per Wetterauer Zeitung). The layoff didn't show.

First pro loss. His takedown attempts against Karlos Vémola ended with him on his back, he was taken down again in R2 and stopped by ground and pound at 4:50. His first opponent with a top-level résumé (previous five opponents went in 7-1, 6-2, 6-7, 0-0 and 1-0).
Used takedowns to control Marc Diakiese, landing hard elbows from top and nearly finishing an RNC in R1. Won 30-27 on all three cards against a UFC veteran.
Controlled on the ground by Fedor Duric in R1 (elbows, near RNC) and lost every round 30-27. His takedown defence held up better in R2.
Stand & Bang (striking-only) rules, not MMA: dropped Dominic Schober three times for a TKO at 2:53 of R1 in his first bout in small gloves. Appeared to hurt his hand.
Stand & Bang (striking-only) rules: dropped three times by debutant Edmon Avagyan and stopped at 2:53 of R1. Follows KO/TKO losses to Daniel Ligocki (2025) and Andreas Gustafsson (2023).
Knocked out Hugo Vach (8-1, on a five-fight win streak) with one hard right hand in R1 after a five-minute power cut. His earlier stoppage losses were all submissions, not strikes.
First stoppage loss: KO'd by one hard right hand from Deniz Ilbay in R1 (2:23). His five-fight streak came against opponents who went in 5-1, 3-0, 2-1, 1-0 and 3-0.
Chopped Robert Pukač's lead leg with low kicks, shook off a brief takedown and closed his left eye with punches for a TKO at 3:55 of R1. His fifth straight finish.

Stopped in R1 by Jaime Cordero's leg kicks and punches; his left eye swelled shut (fightlive.sk reports a likely orbital fracture). His first stoppage loss in his last ten fights; check his injury status before his next booking.
Caught Nikola Janković's takedown attempt in a triangle choke off his back at 1:24 of R1. Now 6-0 with every win in R1, four of them by submission.
Shot a takedown on Tamerlan Dulatov and got caught in a triangle at 1:24 of R1, his first fight in 602 days.
Swept all three rounds on all three cards (30-27 x3) against 13-6 veteran Roman Paulus, and stays unbeaten at 10-0. Better late again.
Dropped the unbeaten Oskar Staszczak early and finished him with follow-up punches at 1:04 of R1. He climbed the cage to celebrate before the referee had stopped it and had to come back to finish.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Lost 29-28 x3 to Ailin Perez despite out-landing her 46-37 in significant strikes; 4 of 6 media scores (MMADecisions) had Dumont winning. The loss is closer than the record shows.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Won R1 and R3 on control (3:41 vs 0:40) while being out-landed 37-46. Official 29-28 x3, but 4 of 6 media scored it for Norma Dumont. A thin win.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Submitted by a standing guillotine at 0:57 of R1 by two-days'-notice replacement Luis Hernandez. His third straight submission loss (McVey, Donte Johnson, Hernandez).

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Won the TUF 34 strawweight final: floored the unbeaten Melissa Amaya with two right hands in R1, then dropped her again with a right hook and multi-punch burst and finished her with hammerfists at 3:19 of R2.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: First pro loss: dropped by two right hands in R1 and stopped in R2 by Tina Black's punches.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Gave up his back while rolling in R2; Brady Hiestand locked a body triangle and finished a rear-naked choke at 4:07.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Dropped Christian Edwards with a left hook in R1 and hunted an RNC, but Edwards took R2 on two of Sherdog's three cards and floored him with a left hook for a TKO at 1:47 of R3. He faded after a strong first round.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Got early takedowns on Elves Brener but faded, then faceplanted from a right hook and was stopped at 4:14 of R1. His second straight R1 KO/TKO loss (Jacobe Smith, Feb 2026).

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Took Montel Jackson down in R1, but was dazed by repeated one-twos and stopped at 2:39 of R2. His second KO/TKO loss since 2023 (Song Yadong).

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Won R1 and R2 on the feet with leg kicks and stance switches, then was taken down twice in R3 and lost a split decision. All 7 media scores (MMADecisions) had him winning 29-28, so treat the loss as a robbery, not decline.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Trailed after two rounds but two R3 takedowns swung two judges for a split decision over John Castaneda. Every media scorer (7 of 7) had Castaneda, so the win flatters him.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Pinned to the fence and knocked out by Yazmin Jauregui's hooks at 1:02 of R1, her first KO/TKO loss.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Taken down easily by Rodolfo Vieira and accepted bottom position; low energy through rounds 1–2. Lost 30-27 on all three cards even though he was better on the feet in round 3.
notes.source: Suleman's fight notes; UFC.com official scorecards

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Took Robert Bryczek down at will and banked rounds 1–2 on control; unanimous 30-27 win against a heavy-handed striker.
notes.source: Suleman's fight notes; UFC.com official scorecards

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Lost the TUF 34 bantamweight final by disqualification (illegal knee, R1 2:19). He wasn't beaten in the fight itself — the model treats it as a non-competitive result, not a real loss.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Won the TUF 34 final by disqualification (illegal knee from Osmanli, R1 2:19). Not counted as a competitive win.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Went deep into a five-round main event and still finished Raoni Barcelos (TKO, R5 1:38). The gas tank holds up over 25 minutes.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Took Rosas into the fifth round before a late TKO at age 39. His résumé going in — five straight UFC wins over Payton Talbott (11-0), Cody Garbrandt, Ricky Simon and Montel Jackson — deserved more weight than the age-curve read gave it.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Stopped Rodolfo Bellato with punches late (TKO R3 1:47) as a clear underdog — finishing power holds into round 3.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: KO'd Vanessa Demopoulos with punches in 62 seconds.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Standing guillotine finish of Sedriques Dumas in 57 seconds on his UFC debut.

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: Rear-naked choke of Rinya Nakamura (R2 4:07).

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: KO'd Ricky Simon with punches (R2 2:39).

notes.event: UFC Fight Night: Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos
notes.note: TKO of Josiah Harrell with a punch (R1 4:14).
Gassed from round 2 against Tai Tuivasa and scraped a split decision.
Body work and kicks opened Doo Ho Choi up; overhand right finished it in R1. Veteran finishing power is real.
Stopped in R1 by Pitbull; now has multiple KO losses.
Was losing R1 on the ground to Eduarda Moura, then found a belly-down armbar at 3:22.
